newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine C. Bank seen selling dlrs-traders.
newsitem.headline: Philippine C. Bank seen selling dlrs-traders.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank was seen selling about $40-50 million at 26.275 pesos in early trade on Friday, traders said.
It renewed its selling because foreign funds, which sold heavily in the the local equities market, are still taking out their money, dealers said.
"Foreign funds haven't slowed (from bringing out their money)," a big bank dealer said. "That's why banks are still taking dollars from the Central Bank."
Last Wednesday, the Central Bank was estimated to have sold more than $120 million at 26.375/26.37 pesos.
It stopped selling when the foreign exchange market calmed following the 0.75 percentage-point increase in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 11.0 percent.
The Bank retained its overnight rate at 11.0 percent early on Friday. It was a bank holiday on Thursday.
It also adjusted upward its borrowing rate on the five-day reverse repo to 11.0 from 10.25 percent.
The Central Bank said its interest rate move was to preempt peso speculation and calm the market amidst jitters over possible large outflows from stock market sales.
